inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Thanks for letting us know about the pump impeller issue' when the customer said they could not find the clip; and 'A kinked or blocked drain hose was very likely the cause' when the customer had said the hose was not kinked and the fix was adding a high loop

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'the most likely issue is an obstruction caught in the drain pump' despite the customer stating it drains fully at the end of every cycle and water appears only after draining the sink

blockingLoop.evidence: The blanking plug/trap check was issued verbatim twice ('Was the blanking plug still in or the trap blocked...') while the customer repeatedly asked whether the missing high loop was the issue and got no answer

rationale: The customer volunteered the two key facts early (water appears after draining the sink; hose lies flat with no high loop since the new sink) and asked three times whether the missing loop was the cause, but the assistant never engaged with it, instead pushing a pump impeller check and repeating a spigot/blanking-plug step verbatim. It then confidently diagnosed a drain pump obstruction on a machine that drains fully every cycle, and when the customer fixed it themselves by adding a high loop, the assistant misattributed the cure to a kinked hose. Safety preambles were fine and no part was pushed, but the assistant contributed nothing to the resolution and misdescribed the evidence.
